Pros:
Automatic PA calibration with no test print, using a direct force measurement
Doubles as a high-precision nozzle-contact probe (drop-in Z- endstop)
Open source (MIT), roughly $30, and stocked by community vendors
Mounting footprint compatible with E3D and Voron toolhead ecosystems
USB or I2C; works with Klipper and RepRapFirmware (community plugin)
Description: An open-source (MIT) strain-gauge sensor from Mark Niu / PandaPi3D that measures extruder pressure directly to derive the optimal Pressure Advance value without printing a calibration pattern. The same hardware works as a switch-type nozzle-contact probe on the Z- endstop pin, and connects to Klipper over USB or I2C. Uses a BF350 350Ω strain gauge mounted zero-distance to its PCB for EMI immunity.
Verdict Label: A ~$30 strain-gauge module that auto-calibrates Pressure Advance without a test print and doubles as a nozzle probe.
Cons:
Requires wiring and Klipper module setup — not plug-and-play
Calibration algorithm is still experimental and evolving
Often sold out at Western vendors
No published accuracy spec for the PA result
Name: bd_pressure

Accuracy (mm): 0.5µm resolution; <350nm typical std dev (documented by Beacon3D)
Pros: Sub-micron resolution (0.5µm); full bed mesh in ~20 seconds without Z motion; integrated ADXL accelerometer rated to 115°C; Contact probe mode (<30g force) for automatic Z-offset without additional hardware; low thermal drift with active temperature compensation; 3.3g lightweight; Normal and Low Profile form factors for different toolheads
Description: Eddy current surface scanner and contact probe combo. RevH is the current production revision with high-temp accelerometer (115°C standby), improved ESD and reverse-polarity protection, and -40% thermal drift vs prior revisions. Scans at 1kHz bandwidth at up to 500mm/s. Contact probe feature uses direct nozzle-touch sensing (<30g) for auto Z-offset with no additional hardware. Ships in Normal (Stealthburner/Annex) and Low Profile (VzBot/RatRig/K3 Frostbite) form factors. Firmware: Klipper and Kalico.
Verdict Label: Voron community standard for precision meshing and auto Z-offset
Cons: Requires conductive bed surface (steel/WHAM BAM/PEI-laminated, ≥400µm); incompatible with large fixed magnets in bed stack; BTT Pi and BTT Manta SBCs require inline USB hub (violates warranty otherwise); $80+ price point is highest among common Voron probes
Name: Beacon RevH

Pros:
Direct nozzle-to-bed contact sensing = zero probe offset from the nozzle tip; no Z-offset recalibration after a nozzle change
High-sensitivity ADS131M02 pressure sensor (24-bit ADC, 64 kHz sampling per Mellow docs) for stable, repeatable triggering
Very cheap at $13.75 with a compact CNC-aluminum top-mount on the heatsink that takes minimal space
Works with Klipper, Marlin and RRF; threshold tuning via USB without firmware changes
5.0 rating from 9 reviews on Mellow's own store page
Description: ALPS pressure module for Goliath hotends that enables automatic Z-axis homing and mesh bed leveling through real-time pressure sensing. Based on the high-sensitivity ADS131M02 sensor, it detects nozzle-to-bed contact with high precision, mounts directly on top of the heatsink in CNC aluminum, and needs no Z-offset recalibration after a nozzle change.
Verdict Label: Cheap nozzle-touch leveling add-on, but Goliath hotends only and thinly field-proven.
Cons:
Goliath hotends only — useless without a Goliath heatsink, so applicability is narrow
No published accuracy or repeatability spec (Accuracy field is 'Unknown')
Requires nozzle wiping for accuracy and secure mounting to avoid vibration issues; multiple leveling tests needed at first setup
Must be wired to the mainboard/toolboard — Type-C alone will not run it, so wiring and Klipper config are required
Small community footprint vs Klicky, Voron Tap and Beacon; thinly field-proven
Name: ALPS Pressure Sensor Module

Pros:
Real-time Z adjustment without waiting for a bed mesh before every print
Lightning-fast bed meshing with no Z-axis up/down moves per point
Only a 1.5 g coil sits on the toolhead — the lightest eddy probe; PCB mounts remotely
High-temperature chamber ready (120°C rated), since all electronics sit away from the hotend
CAN bus supported; works with Klipper and Marlin
Nozzle collision sensing gives auto Z-offset and overcomes temperature drift of the mesh
$28.99 — far cheaper than Beacon/Cartographer eddy probes
Description: Open-source eddy current distance sensor from Mark Niu / PandaPi3D that measures bed distance in real time without moving the Z axis up and down, enabling fast bed meshing and live Z-offset adjustment during printing. The M variant puts only a 1.5 g shielded coil on the toolhead (1.8mm cable) with the PCB mounted remotely, so it suits high-temperature chambers up to 120°C. Nozzle collision sensing (±0.005mm repeatability) gives automatic Z-offset calibration and a mesh that does not drift with temperature. Connects via GPIO/I2C or CAN bus; works with Klipper and Marlin. Requires a conductive bed surface.
Verdict Label: Budget eddy probe with real-time Z compensation and a 1.5 g coil for hot chambers; still a niche Klipper project
Cons:
Requires a conductive bed surface (steel/PEI-laminated); invisible to glass or Garolite
Klipper module and wiring setup — not plug-and-play; EXP1 pin order must be checked and only one connector used
Short-term preorder at Fabreeko (ships in 7–10 days); small community vs Beacon/Cartographer
Published ±0.005mm figure is contact-mode repeatability; no standalone eddy-distance accuracy published
Stiff 1.8mm coaxial cable to the remote coil must not be bent sharply
Name: BD Sensor M

Pros:
No moving parts — nothing to wear out or crash into the bed
Temperature-stable design in the Prusa lineage: no thermistor or compensation table needed (per Prusa KB)
Excellent repeatability per Fabreeko listing
Only $14.99 — cheapest probe on this table
Simple 5V, 3-wire connection; proven on FYSETC's MK3S+ and Mini+ clone kits
Description: FYSETC's 5V inductive bed probe, a SuperPINDA-compatible replacement used in FYSETC's MK3S+ and Mini+ clone kits. It follows Prusa's SuperPINDA design: an inductive sensor that reads the steel sheet under the build plate with no moving parts, and — per Prusa — needs no thermistor because its components are temperature-stable enough not to require compensation. It acts as the Z endstop and mesh-bed-leveling sensor. Requires a metal bed surface; trigger height is set with a zip-tie gauge. A budget clone of a proven Prusa part, not a genuine Prusa sensor.
Verdict Label: Cheap clone of Prusa's proven SuperPINDA; fine for Prusa-style builds with steel sheets, but a niche pick for CoreXY builds
Cons:
Only works with a metal/steel sheet under the build surface — invisible to glass, Garolite or thick BuildTak
Clone quality and temperature stability unverified against the genuine Prusa SuperPINDA
Currently out of stock at Fabreeko
No accuracy figure published by FYSETC
Short sensing distance — height must be set precisely with a zip-tie gauge
Niche for this database: inductive probes are largely superseded by eddy probes in Voron/CoreXY builds
Name: Super Pinda

Accuracy (mm): Accuracy not published; ADXL345-based; probe specs unconfirmed
Pros: Integrates ADXL345 accelerometer with eddy current probe functionality; BTT-ecosystem-adjacent with Fly3D CAN toolhead boards; Klipper native; compact form factor suited to Fly SHT and SB2040-series toolhead boards
Description: ADXL345-based probe module from Mellow (Fly3D), a Chinese Klipper hardware manufacturer. Mellow produces CAN toolhead boards (Fly-SHT36, Fly-SB2040) that include integrated ADXL345 sensors. The Fly-ADXL product combines accelerometer (for input shaping) with probe functionality for bed meshing. Details on standalone probe performance are sparse in Western community sources. Requires verification against current Mellow product lineup before recommending — Mellow's product naming evolves rapidly.
Verdict Label: Niche Klipper ecosystem option; limited English documentation — needs verification
Cons: Limited English-language documentation; smaller install base than Beacon, Cartographer, or BTT Eddy; product specifications not independently verified; Mellow Fly ecosystem is less common in Western Voron community; record needs spec verification
Name: Fly ADXL

Accuracy (mm): Eddy current displacement; accuracy not independently published by BTT
Pros: Budget-friendly eddy current in the BTT ecosystem; USB and CAN bus versions available; integrates with BTT toolhead boards; Klipper support via BTT's open source firmware; competitive price vs Cartographer
Description: BTT's eddy current displacement sensor for bed meshing and homing. Part of BigTreeTech's ecosystem of Klipper hardware. Available in USB and CAN variants. Targets the same use case as Beacon and Cartographer at a budget price point. BTT maintains open source firmware. Community adoption is growing but lags significantly behind Beacon RevH and Cartographer V3/V4 in documented installations and community guides. Requires conductive bed surface.
Verdict Label: Budget eddy current option; Cartographer is better established at similar price
Cons: Requires conductive bed; accuracy specs not published; mixed community reception on reliability; BTT hardware RF interference with BTT Pi and Manta boards (same issue as Beacon — likely worse given BTT hardware pairing); smaller community and documentation base than Beacon or Cartographer; newer/less field-proven
Name: Eddy

Pros: Works with all bed materials (glass, metal, wood, PEI); widely supported across Klipper and Marlin; self-test and alarm functions on power-up; blue/red LED wiring diagnostics; well-documented with printer-specific wiring guides; no bed conductivity requirement
Description: Hall effect auto bed leveling sensor using a solenoid-actuated push pin and hall sensor. BLTouch Smart V3.1 is the current production version, made by ANTCLABS (Seoul, South Korea). Works with all bed materials by sensing pin retraction rather than bed conductivity. Industry standard on entry-level Cartesian printers (Ender series, CR-10, etc.). Largely replaced by Tap, Klicky, and eddy probes in the self-build CoreXY community.
Verdict Label: Viable on Cartesian printers; outclassed in CoreXY/Voron builds
Cons: Servo mechanism subject to wear over time; less repeatable than eddy current or magnetic dock probes; not a standard in Voron/CoreXY builds; widespread counterfeiting (3D Touch, TL Touch clones — genuine requires QR code on PCB); must be mounted exactly perpendicular to bed
Name: BL Touch

Accuracy (mm): <0.025mm range; ~0.01mm std dev (per project README; community-measured)
Pros: Extremely low cost (<$15 self-build BOM); fully open source (GPL-3.0); no bed material restrictions; automated dock/undock via Klipper macros; 1.4k GitHub stars, active community; KlickyNG variant adds self-aligning enclosed magnets (no glue required); compatible with klipper_z_calibration plugin
Description: Magnetically attached microswitch probe for CoreXY printers. Uses 6x3mm neodymium magnets for both mechanical attachment and electrical contact. Klicky PCB is the PCB-based variant for improved repeatability. KlickyNG is the current recommended revision with self-aligning, enclosed magnet slots that don't require glue. Klipper macros automate probe attach and detach sequences during homing. Voron community staple since ~2021, increasingly superseded by Beacon RevH in new builds.
Verdict Label: Best-value probe for Voron builds; community staple with proven reliability
Cons: Requires printed dock, toolhead mount, and dock mount specific to each printer model; Klipper macro configuration overhead; slower than eddy probes (sequential point-by-point probing); losing popularity to Beacon RevH in new Voron builds; needs recalibration after printer geometry changes
Name: Klicky PCB

Accuracy (mm): Eddy current displacement; accuracy not independently published by manufacturer
Pros: Budget-friendly eddy current (~$30 V3, ~$40 V4); USB+CAN dual protocol; built-in ADXL345 for input shaping; Survey Touch contact probe mode (V3+); multiple form factors (standard, flat-pack, low-profile, right-angle); V4 AIO integrates all features in one revised board
Description: Eddy current induction sensor for bed meshing and homing. V3 ($29.99) ships with ADXL345 and dual USB/CAN support. Survey Touch (contact probe mode) added in V3 for nozzle-touch Z-offset. V4 ($39.99) is a revised AIO board. Form factors include Standard, Flat Pack, Low Profile, and Right-Angle to suit VzBot, RatRig, and Voron toolheads. Uses a Klipper plugin for firmware integration. Strong budget alternative to Beacon RevH.
Verdict Label: Best-value eddy current probe; strong Beacon alternative at ~1/3 the price
Cons: Requires conductive bed; accuracy specs not officially published; Survey Touch calibration adds setup steps; mixed community reports on edge-of-bed accuracy; V4 is newer and less field-proven than V3; smaller install base than Beacon
Name: Cartographer

Accuracy (mm): Microswitch-based; accuracy not independently published by manufacturer
Pros: PCB with screw-attached magnets ensures dimensional accuracy and repeatable attachment; works with all bed materials and surface treatments regardless of temperature or magnetism; multi-firmware support (Klipper, Marlin, RRF2, RRF3, Smoothie); high-temp variant rated to 125°C+ for enclosed hot chambers; 5V and 24V native versions; well-documented printer-specific dock and mount guides
Description: Magnetically coupled microswitch Z-probe for 3D printers, lasers, and CNC machines. PCB uses screw-attached magnets for both mechanical coupling and electrical contacts, delivering more precise and reliable attachment than printed magnet holders. Works regardless of bed material, magnetism, or surface treatment. Rated to 80°C natively; high-temp variants rated to 125°C+ available directly. Available as DIY build or kit via authorized resellers. Supports Klipper, Marlin, RRF2/3, and Smoothie.
Verdict Label: Solid alternative to Klicky; better hardware finish but smaller Voron community footprint
Cons: Less Voron-community-centric than Klicky; requires dock, wiring, and macro configuration; slower than eddy probes; project development pace is notably slower; CC BY-NC-SA license restricts commercial use of designs; smaller reseller network than Klicky
Name: Euclid Probe

Pros:
Hotend and probe in one purchase ($62.40) — replaces a BLTouch/3D Touch and a hotend at the same time
High-performance hotend: 96W ceramic heater, up to 350 C with PT1000 sensor, over 40 mm3/s flow, TC4 titanium heat break
Direct nozzle-touch leveling via the integrated ADS131M02 ALPS module (24-bit ADC, 64 kHz sampling, 128x gain, Kalman filtering) — no Z-offset recalibration after nozzle changes
USB plug-and-play threshold tuning on a PC, no coding or firmware tweaks required
Standard V6 nozzle compatibility (copper, hardened steel, tungsten carbide, silicon carbide) and Klipper/Marlin/RRF support
5.0 rating from 15 reviews on Mellow's own store page
Description: Compact high-performance V6 hotend with a 96W ceramic heater (up to 350 C with PT1000 sensor, over 40 mm3/s flow) that integrates Mellow's ALPS pressure-based bed leveling module, which detects nozzle-to-bed contact via the ADS131M02 sensor for auto Z homing and mesh leveling. V6 nozzle compatible; works with Klipper, Marlin and RRF; sold as a BLTouch/3D Touch replacement for Voron, BLV, VzBot and HevORT DIY printers.
Verdict Label: High-flow V6 hotend with nozzle-touch leveling built in; promising but new and unproven at scale.
Cons:
ALPS pressure accuracy/repeatability is not published (Accuracy field is 'Unknown') — no independent verification of the leveling precision
Not suitable for easily deformable heated beds or X-axes prone to deformation/distortion, per Mellow's own manual
New integrated product with a small community footprint; far less field-proven than Beacon, Cartographer or Voron Tap
Bigger install than a probe alone — a full hotend swap plus ALPS wiring (1.5 m cable to mainboard UART) and threshold calibration
Listing also sells 2.85 mm-oriented variants/sets, so buyers must pick the right filament-diameter set
Name: FluxHeat V6 ALPS Nozzle Probe

Accuracy (mm): Optical switch-based; accuracy not independently published; similar to BLTouch in practice
Pros: Drop-in upgrade for Creality printers; uses metal probe pin vs BLTouch's plastic pin (more durable); optical sensor vs hall effect (less susceptible to magnetic interference); works with all bed materials; cheaper than BLTouch; Klipper support via bltouch config section
Description: Creality's proprietary bed leveling probe, functionally similar to BLTouch. Uses an optical sensor to detect pin retraction rather than a hall effect sensor. Metal push pin is more durable than BLTouch's engineering plastic pin. Designed as an OEM upgrade for Creality printers (Ender 3 V2, CR-10 series, etc.). Configures in Klipper via the bltouch configuration section. Rarely used outside of Creality-ecosystem builds; irrelevant for Voron, RatRig, or VzBot builds.
Verdict Label: Creality ecosystem only; irrelevant for Voron/RatRig/VzBot builds
Cons: Creality-ecosystem focused — limited mount options for CoreXY/Voron builds; not meaningful for self-build prosumer printers; Creality-branded and primarily shipped with Creality printers; lacks the established community documentation of BLTouch for third-party use
Name: CR Touch

Accuracy (mm): 0.1µm std dev; 6µm range over 100 probes (E3D test)
Pros:
Nozzle itself is the probe — zero XY offset and no Z-offset recalibration after a nozzle change
Excellent repeatability in E3D's testing: 0.1µm std dev over 100 probes, 15,000-cycle durability test
Works with any bed surface (contact sensing, no conductivity requirement)
Lightweight, compact washer + board; adds little toolhead mass vs Voron Tap
Configurable via UART/I2C with 5 presets, threshold and IIR filter tuning
Klipper and Duet support; usable as X, Y or Z probe or for tool-offset measurement on a tool changer
Description: E3D's compact piezoelectric bed-levelling and Z-homing system. A piezo washer mounted behind the hotend (or factory-fitted into the Revo Voron heatsink in the Voron edition) converts mechanical strain into an electrical charge when the nozzle touches the bed, so the nozzle itself is the probe — no XY offset and no Z-offset recalibration after a nozzle change. The included PZ Probe Board outputs an active-low switch-style trigger and is configurable in 5 presets via UART or I2C (threshold, IIR filter), with trigger on compression or expansion of the piezo element. Works with Klipper and Duet (RepRapFirmware); the standalone kit lets you integrate contact probing into setups beyond the Revo ecosystem, including X/Y/Z probing or tool-offset measurement on a tool changer. Note: it cannot be integrated into a standard Revo Voron sink — Voron users need the Coldside kit. 5V maximum; max ambient 75°C.
Verdict Label: Piezo nozzle-contact probe with excellent repeatability; fiddly tuning keeps it a niche pick
Cons:
Not plug-and-play — requires sensitivity/preset tuning and can suffer false triggering or no triggering (motor vibration, fan/heater noise, probing speed, plastic on the nozzle)
Strict 5V maximum; exceeding it can cause serious damage, and bed damage during probing is not covered under warranty
Cannot be integrated into a standard Revo Voron sink — Voron users need the separate Coldside kit
Washer needs precise ~1Nm preload torque and hard, smooth mating surfaces; a loose screw causes inconsistent probing
Nozzle must be clean and probed ~50°C below print temperature to avoid oozing-related mis-triggers
Currently sold out on E3D Online (product page shows 'Sold out')
Name: PZ Probe

Accuracy (mm): Direct nozzle-touch; repeatability not published; community-measured ~1-5µm std dev typical
Pros: Direct nozzle contact = zero probe offset from nozzle tip; works with any bed surface (textured PEI, smooth, magnetic sheets); fully integrated into Stealthburner/CW2 toolhead; open source Voron project; r2 revision resolved documented r1 PCB reliability issues; no separate probe dock required
Description: Optical endstop triggered by nozzle deflection, integrated into the Stealthburner toolhead for Voron 2.4 and Trident. XY linear rails allow the toolhead to physically travel downward when the nozzle contacts the bed, triggering an internal optical sensor. r1 was the original release with documented PCB issues; r2 is the current recommended revision with improved PCB and updated magnet arrangement. Voron community verdict: Tap delivers accurate Z-offset via direct nozzle sensing, but Beacon RevH is now preferred by most new builders for combined eddy mesh + contact Z calibration with less setup complexity.
Verdict Label: Accurate nozzle-touch Z; installation complexity has pushed most new Voron builders to Beacon
Cons: Requires Stealthburner toolhead — not compatible with other toolhead designs (Xol, Dragon Burner, etc.); installation involves precise spring tensioning and gantry configuration; nozzle thermal expansion causes Z reading drift unless compensated; r1 PCBs had documented optical sensor failures; slower bed mesh than eddy probes (sequential point-by-point); cumulative nozzle wear from repeated touch cycles
Name: Voron Tap
